title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID (Rodrigo Diaz, died 1099, Castile) placed as a caravan figure - wrong century and wrong region by nearly two hundred years; he is used to stand in for a 13th-century Venetian merchant
WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR (died 1087, Normandy/England) placed in the Polo caravan - an 11th-century Norman king has no business on the 1271 Silk Road
GENGHIS_KHAN placed as a GAIA object at the destination: Genghis died in 1227 and the Polos were received by his grandson Kublai Khan, whose hero unit exists in the editor and should have been used
KNIGHT x3 as caravan escort - heavy Latin-Christian shock cavalry crossing Persia and the Pamirs is implausible; camel riders or light cavalry escorts were available in the engine
SHEEP x6 standing in for the caravan's pack animals when TRADE_CART and camel units were available and far more representative of a Silk Road caravan
CASTLE/KEEP used to represent Shangdu, giving the Khan's summer palace generic European stone-fortress architecture; a Wonder or pagoda-style structure would have read better
